articles.title_orig: China posts weakest industrial profit growth this year, expanding 4.2% in August
articles.title_zh: China posts weakest industrial profit growth this year, expanding 4.2% in August
articles.content_orig:
China's industrial profits grew 4.2% in August from a year earlier, official data released Monday showed, as manufacturers grapple with persistent weakness in consumer demand and a sustained rise in energy costs.
For the first eight months of this year, profits at large industrial firms climbed 15.7%, easing from a 17.6% rise in the January-July period . That would mark the fourth straight month of deceleration from the 24.7% pace set in April .
While growth has been slowing, industrial earnings have staged a notable reversal this year, swinging from a barely-positive 0.6% gain for all of 2025 — the first increase after three straight years of declines — to double-digit growth. That expansion has been led by the artificial-intelligence-fueled boom in chips and computing equipment and has coincided with the end of nearly three years of factory-gate deflation.
Profits at the computer, communication and electronic equipment manufacturing industry more than doubled for the January-to-August period, rising 110% from a year earlier. The automobile manufacturing industry, however, saw profits drop by 16% during the same period as the sector sees cut-throat competition.
Dragged by tepid consumer demand, growth in the world's second-largest economy softened to its slowest pace in more than three years in the second quarter.
The official purchasing managers' index indicated that manufacturing activity contracted for two consecutive months in July and August. Retail sales slowed further , and the urban investment slump deepened in August, while industrial output rebounded on the back of exports.
Economists expect Beijing to lean harder on stimulus to stabilize corporate profitability, as consolidation accelerates in sectors already facing sluggish demand, fierce competition and cutthroat price wars.

articles.title_orig: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says
articles.title_zh: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says
articles.content_orig:
David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island
Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.
David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”
The extraordinary claim came during an interview about US policy on Taiwan, which has been waiting for months for Trump to approve a new arms sales ⁠package worth $14bn , after a record multi-billion dollar deal was unveiled in December last year.
Trump’s level of commitment to protecting Taiwan has previously been questioned . At a meeting with Xi in Beijing in May, ⁠Trump said he was keeping the $14bn Taiwan arms sales package in abeyance, describing it as a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China.
Washington has long maintained a strategically ambiguous stance on whether it would defend Taiwan in the event of an invasion. But under the decades-old Taiwan Relations Act, it is required to provide Taipei with sufficient military equipment to defend itself.
Beijing has repeatedly said it “resolutely opposes” Washington’s arms sales to the island democracy, which it regards as a breakaway province, despite never having ruled it, and has not renounced the use of force to take. During their Washington meeting last week, Xi urged Trump to oppose “Taiwan independence,” according to a readout from the official Chinese news agency Xinhua.
After Purdue’s interview, the White House told the New York Times that the US had no plans to sell arms to China , while the state department said: “US law prohibits arms sales to China and there is no offer or plan to sell arms to China.”
Before the interview, Taiwanese deputy foreign minister Chen Ming-chi spoke of the severe military threat China posed.
“Taiwan faces a severe situation in the Taiwan strait. Even though China’s economy is declining, it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under ‌this context, the US very much understands our defence needs,” he told reporters in Taipei.
Trump ​has not mentioned the sale ‌since last week’s summit, saying ‌only on Saturday that Xi understands his position on Taiwan.
Perdue himself told CNBC ​on Friday that there had been ​no change in Taiwan policy by Trump, including on arms ​sales.

President Trump talks with members of the media on September 16, 2026. Photo: Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images.
President Trump was inaudible during a press conference Monday after the TV pool suspended coverage, with White House-provided video carrying no usable audio of his remarks.
Why it matters: It's a remarkable and immediate ramification of Trump's attempt to limit pool access.
Driving the news: President Trump announced a ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico on Friday, confiscating their credentials on Saturday over what he termed "FAKE NEWS".
Thought bubble, via Axios' Brittany Gibson, one of the poolers: The White House Press Pool, by design and by necessity, is a collaborative effort amongst the nation's top news outlets.
How it works: The White House press pool is a rotating group of journalists who stay by the president's side throughout his public appearances and share their reporting, audio and footage with the rest of the media.
The big picture: Trump is constantly on the move, so the pool makes it easier and less expensive to document his whereabouts.
What they're saying: "So this isn't just DC insider access journalism," Seth Stern, chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation, tells Axios.
Zoom in: "The president is a walking news story," Stern says.
Without a TV pool crew, there is little independent broadcast video of the president's restricted-access events.
The bottom line: The TV pool gives the public an independent audiovisual record of presidential events that otherwise may be seen only through government-provided cameras.

articles.content_orig:
Are you ready to celebrate the year's top music videos? Tonight, music's biggest, brightest and most promising artists are gathering at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards .
From fit checks to performances to culture-shaping confrontations, the VMAs have consistently been the site for some of pop culture's most noteworthy moments. This year's awards show, hosted by Snoop Dogg , is expected to be one for the books .
Three of pop music's most influential names will be celebrated for their remarkable contributions to the genre — and industry — they helped define: Madonna, the Queen of Pop, will return to the VMAs main stage for the first time in over two decades; " Patient Zero " pop star Taylor Swift will make history as the first-ever recipient of the Artist Director Honors; and late, beloved singer George Michael will be honored during a star-studded performance.
Kacey Musgraves is also set to take the stage for a special tribute to Dolly Parton. As if those weren't enough reasons to celebrate, female artists are also leading this year's crop of nominees .
Want the play-by-play? Follow along for Yahoo Entertainment's live coverage below.
Photo illustration: Yahoo News
The VMAs were set to air at 7:30 p.m. ET, but turns out viewers are going to have to wait for the end of the Ravens-Cowboys game to catch the action:
The show is happening, according to our reporters in the room. Madonna has already performed. We just can't see anything until the game is over.
Fashionably late? When you're Taylor Swift, everyone else is simply early. The singer was the last star to hit the VMAs carpet, arriving just minutes before showtime in a sleek black halter bodysuit that gave way to a draped, sparkling silver skirt. She also kept her blunt, shoulder-skimming cut — a look that she debuted just ahead of releasing The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore .
Taylor Swift shuts down the red carpet.
Tonight is very much Swift's night. She'll receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors, which will officially make her the most-awarded artist in VMAs history, while the music video for her new single "Patient Zero" will premiere during the show.
To put it simply: It's Mrs. Kelce's world and we're all just living in it.
Tonight's show hasn't started yet, but the best looks from the VMAs have definitely arrived. The early trends from the red carpet strike a balance between retrospective and current, ranging from an homage to the inaugural show in 1984 to a bold twist on a major trend of the moment. Here's what we're seeing and loving.
In honor of Madonna's return to the VMAs stage tonight, black lace, drastic hemlines, chunky cross jewelry and slogan belts are taking center stage on the carpet.
Bebe Rexha perfectly pays homage to Madonna's iconic look from the inaugural awards show with layers of black lace and a two-bra corset top that Rexha confirmed was inspired by the Queen of Pop.
Bella Kay definitely got the fashion memo and spun it with a choker necklace, combat boots and chunky turquoise jewelry.
Sombr's in-your-face message belt is a not-so-subtle nod to Madge's 1984 VMAs performance. Instead of "Boy Toy," he went with "Sex." Straight to the point.
Teyana Taylor's floor-length gown definitely fits the bill. The long feather trim and oversized fishnet pattern make it one of the boldest looks of the night.
Seeing double? Sophie Silva's outfit is the most exact take on the trend, down to the "Boy Toy" belt.
Yee — and I cannot emphasize this enough — haw . Western wear is all over the red carpet, from cowboy hats to leather touches and corset pants (you read that right).
Orville Peck is giving Zorro-meets-John-Wayne in this masked, fringed leather getup.
Madisin Rian's cowhide look is one of the more intense takes on the trend, and I'm extremely here for it.
Chanel West Coast nails a few trends with this one: high-low hemline, lace, leopard and a bold cowboy hat.
Ciara Miller trades a corset top for a leather bra; her pants, however, make up for it with laces that run from hip to toe.
It wouldn't be the VMAs if there wasn't an ungodly amount of skin showing. These celebs are baring it all for the event.
JoJo's bedazzled black set is neither Too Little nor Too Late.
Charli xcx lets her torso do the talking in an otherwise understated black number. I don't care, I love it.
Tyla's reptilian set quite literally has me lost for words.
Nezza defies logic with a full-length gown that still showcases her entire midsection.
Who just walked by me? Taylor Swift, who will be debuting her "Patient Zero" music video tonight.
Spotted: Charli xcx, who definitely yielded the loudest screams on the carpet. She was moved quickly and did not come down the line for interviews, but I did manage to catch a quick glimpse. My immediate thought: Girl rocks a smoky eye so well.
By taking home the inaugural Artist Director Honors tonight, Taylor Swift is officially the most-awarded artist in VMAs history, surpassing Beyoncé, with whom she was previously tied.
"Across her work, Swift has brought an increasingly expansive approach to storytelling, creating interconnected narratives, cinematic worlds and recurring details that invite audiences deeper into each project," said a press release for Swift's major award. "The inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors recognizes that body of work, while also underscoring the growing role artists play in shaping how their music is brought to life on screen."
On Friday, executive producer Bruce Gillmer told the Associated Press that the award was an "extension" of the Video Vanguard Award, which this year is going to Nirvana. That award is a lifetime achievement honor given to musicians and directors who have made a significant impact on the music video art form.
Gillmer added that "the kernel of the idea" for the new Artist Director Honors "came from external."
He said that the VMAs team put a lot of work into "crafting and thinking about what this could be, the importance of it, [and] launching something as big or bigger than Vanguard."
Swift, who has directed many of her own music videos, has not received the Vanguard award.
It's safe to say Paris Hilton has never met a sequin she didn't like — her iconic 21st birthday dress remains in my brain for all eternity — and tonight she wore all of them. She walked the teal carpet in head-to-toe sparkle: a short, sparkly silver minidress with cutouts, thigh-high boots and matching gloves. And that sleek, sharp-as-a-knife bob is seriously bobbin'! (Hilton is also presenting at tonight's ceremony. )

Her sister, Nicky Hilton Rothschild, joined her on the carpet in a floor-length, silver sparkly gown, making it a coordinated sister-style moment. That's hot.

articles.title_zh: 49ers lose Mike Evans with rib injury
articles.content_orig:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans has been knocked out of today’s game with a rib injury.
Evans took a hard hit while catching a pass in the second quarter and walked off the field in obvious pain. Once he got to the sideline he went to the ground and had to be helped to a cart and taken to the locker room.
When healthy, the 33-year-old Evans has been among the best wide receivers in the NFL for years, but he’s had a hard time staying healthy recently. Last year he missed most of the season with a string of injuries that included a hamstring strain, a concussion and a broken collarbone. He also missed time the year before with a hamstring injury. Now the 49ers will hope he can recover from his rib injury soon.
The 49ers were also without cornerback Deommodore Lenoir for much of the first half while he was evaluated for a concussion, but Lenoir was cleared and returned in the second half.
Despite the injuries, the 49ers keep rolling and are leading the Cardinals 17-6 in the third quarter.

articles.title_orig: 5 arrested in U.K. near base used by U.S. on suspicion of planning terror act
articles.title_zh: 5 arrested in U.K. near base used by U.S. on suspicion of planning terror act
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in western England.
The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base, and arrested five men “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act.” They were later further charged on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
Police did not provide further details on the men, who remain in custody, or what they were suspected to have done. “Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing,” Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans of Counter Terrorism Policing said the force is “working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident,” with the investigation still in its “early stages.”
Ocone said 85 homes across the local area were evacuated and a 440-yard cordon put in place while an Army ordnance disposal team examines the vehicles.
Helicopter footage from Sky News showed multiple white vans close to the base seemingly being searched by a bomb disposal robot.
Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, told Britain’s Press Association another resident had reported three suspicious vans in the village. Along with other residents, Tudsbery has since been evacuated to a nearby recreation center.
The Reuters news agency had reported that security measures at the air ‌base have been significantly increased in recent ‌days.
Cotswold District Council member Tristan Wilkinson told NBC News that a threat to the base from Iran about six weeks ago has heightened the alert level in the community and led to a ramped-up police presence and an increase in security patrols.
Wilkinson noted there is “a lot more vigilance from the local community” and that police in this instance “have done exactly what you’d hope they would do in increasing reassurance for the community.”
“This is a worry and escalation, and we wait to see what the nature of that actual incident is going to be,” the official added.
A U.S. European Command spokesperson said: “For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”
“U.S. European Command remains vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families across the European theater,” the spokesperson added. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”
Asked about the incident Sunday after walking off Air Force One, President Donald Trump told reporters the arrest was an “amazing job.”
“They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great,” he said.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a post on X: “I know today’s incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country.”
“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” he added.
“The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts,” Burnham said.
In March, Keir Starmer , Burnham’s predecessor, gave permission for the U.S. to use its bases for “specific and limited defensive” operations against Iran.
In July, Iran’s ⁠Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Britain that “any base used to invade Iranian territory is our legitimate target,” Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported, citing bomber aircraft flights from Fairford.
At the time, a British government spokesperson said that the country was “ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad.”
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.
Courtney Kube is a correspondent covering national security and the military for the NBC News Investigative Unit.
Raf Sanchez is a foreign correspondent for NBC News.

articles.content_orig:
The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards wowed audiences on Sunday night as Madonna brought out high-energy dance numbers and Taylor Swift made history.
Here are the highlights from the 2026 VMAs.
Madonna took the VMAs stage at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles, her first time peforming at the award show in over 20 years, announcing: "It's mother."
She opened the show with newly iconic imagery from her recent album, "Confessions II," including green lasers and hordes of cameras following her and Sabrina Carpenter around.
The two performed "Bring Your Love" together, which later won the Best Collaboration award, before Madonna transitioned into another dance-fueled club number, "Danceteria" with Charli XCX. The performance featured appearances from several stars who had cameos in "Confessions II — The Film," including Debi Mazar and Julia Garner.
Madonna later took home Artist of the Year.
Kacey Musgraves paid tribute to Dolly Parton on Sunday after the VMAs played a short video of the late country music superstar. Musgraves sang "I Will Always Love You," a song Parton released in 1974 that took on a second life when it was later recorded by the late Whitney Houston.
Parton, one of the most groundbreaking and successful musicians in the history of country music, died last month after a brief battle with cancer.
K-Pop star LISA performed her new single "SaWaDiKa" in the song's TV debut. Part of the performance included the singer riding in the front of Thailand's iconic tuk-tuk taxi.
Earlier in the night, she accepted the Best Pop award for "Dream feat. Kentaro Sakaguchi."
The surviving members of genre-defining grunge band Nirvana were given the Video Vanguard award, recognizing their contribution to the form.
The tribute included archival footage of late frontman Kurt Cobain discussing the process behind the making of several of the band's videos, including "Smells Like Teen Spirit," "Come As You Are" and "Heart-Shaped Box"
The VMAs also brought a milestone for Taylor Swift , who was given the VMAs' first-ever Artist Director Honor, which organizers said recognizes artists "whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."
Swift thanked her fans and everyone she has ever collaborated with on her music videos. She then premiered the music video for her new single "Patient Zero," which stars Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell.
The new accolade made Swift the show's most-awarded artist ever. She was previously tied with Beyoncé, who has 30 Moon Persons.
Swift also won Video of the Year and was nominated in 10 other categories. Swift paid tribute to Parton in her acceptance speech for the final award of the evening.
Alex  Sundby contributed to this report.

articles.content_orig:
Takeaways from the Giants’ 12-7 win over the Titans at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
1. Well, it was not exactly a nor’easter but it was a windy and wet day for football. There were plenty of empty seats and that was not because Jaxson Dart is out for the season or because the Titans are not a marquee draw. Sometimes, fans do not want to sit out there for three hours in uncomfortable conditions. On the field, the wind did not seem to wreak too much havoc with the passing game — the struggles seemed more about the quarterbacks, Jameis Winston and Cam Ward, than the weather. After the raucous environment two weeks ago for the season-opening victory over the Cowboys, this was a far more subdued afternoon.
Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.
2 .  Malik Nabers looked quite excited, gesturing with full enthusiasm that he picked up the first down on a 12-yard reception on the first play of the Giants’ final possession in the fourth quarter. Nabers made the catch against former teammate Cor’Dale Flott, which must have felt good. As it turned out, that was Nabers’ longest reception of the game. He caught five passes for only 26 yards and was actually the most productive wide receiver (Darnell Mooney had 20 receiving yards and rookie Malachi Fields had 19). It was that sort of sluggish day for the passing attack. Sure, the weather was not conducive for long-range throws but there were enough throws by Jameis Winston that could have been completed that he failed to deliver. Games like this can frustrate wide receivers. It is something to monitor.
3. Coaching matters. Titans head coach Robert Saleh sent Joey Slye out to try a 59-yard field goal with 41 seconds remaining in the first half. Yes, Slye was kicking with the wind and yes, he was hitting them from long distance in the pregame warmup. Still, it was not exactly a high-percentage play. The Titans were down 6-0 so they were right in this low-scoring affair. Punting the ball away would be fine. Slye had the distance but missed wide left, giving the Giants the ball on their 49-yard line. From there, all that was needed was two first downs to set Dominic Zvada up for a 39-yard field goal as time expired. Instead of being down one score, the Titans trailed 9-0. Big difference.

articles.title_orig: Deadly storm hits the Northeast, and five arrested on terrorism charge near a U.S. air base: Weekend Rundown
articles.title_zh: Deadly storm hits the Northeast, and five arrested on terrorism charge near a U.S. air base: Weekend Rundown
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in western England.
The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base, and arrested five men “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act.” They were later further charged on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.
Police did not provide further details on the men, who remain in custody, or what they were suspected to have done. “Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing,” Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans of Counter Terrorism Policing said the force is “working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident,” with the investigation still in its “early stages.”
Ocone said 85 homes across the local area were evacuated and a 440-yard cordon put in place while an Army ordnance disposal team examines the vehicles.
Helicopter footage from Sky News showed multiple white vans close to the base seemingly being searched by a bomb disposal robot.
Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, told Britain’s Press Association another resident had reported three suspicious vans in the village. Along with other residents, Tudsbery has since been evacuated to a nearby recreation center.
The Reuters news agency had reported that security measures at the air ‌base have been significantly increased in recent ‌days.
Cotswold District Council member Tristan Wilkinson told NBC News that a threat to the base from Iran about six weeks ago has heightened the alert level in the community and led to a ramped-up police presence and an increase in security patrols.
Wilkinson noted there is “a lot more vigilance from the local community” and that police in this instance “have done exactly what you’d hope they would do in increasing reassurance for the community.”
“This is a worry and escalation, and we wait to see what the nature of that actual incident is going to be,” the official added.
A U.S. European Command spokesperson said: “For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”
“U.S. European Command remains vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families across the European theater,” the spokesperson added. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”
Asked about the incident Sunday after walking off Air Force One, President Donald Trump told reporters the arrest was an “amazing job.”
“They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great,” he said.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a post on X: “I know today’s incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country.”
“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” he added.
“The investigation remains ongoing, and I would urge people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts,” Burnham said.
In March, Keir Starmer , Burnham’s predecessor, gave permission for the U.S. to use its bases for “specific and limited defensive” operations against Iran.
In July, Iran’s ⁠Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Britain that “any base used to invade Iranian territory is our legitimate target,” Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported, citing bomber aircraft flights from Fairford.
At the time, a British government spokesperson said that the country was “ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad.”
Freddie Clayton is a freelance journalist based in London.
Courtney Kube is a correspondent covering national security and the military for the NBC News Investigative Unit.
Raf Sanchez is a foreign correspondent for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Taxpayer-funded Trump ads draw bipartisan scrutiny ahead of midterms
articles.title_zh: Taxpayer-funded Trump ads draw bipartisan scrutiny ahead of midterms
articles.content_orig:
John Kennedy pushes back against such spending as pro-Trump ‘public service announcements’ air before midterms
As the White House expands a taxpayer-funded advertising campaign to promote Donald Trump ’s political agenda before the November midterm elections , US senator John Kennedy told CBS News on Sunday “there ought to be a rule” against such spending – before tacitly admitting such spending is “probably” illegal.
Kennedy, the US president’s fellow Republican , was asked by Margaret Brennan, the CBS Face the Nation host, about the White House spending to air multiple ads featuring Trump – including one that was produced for his 2024 election campaign.
Brennan first reminded Kennedy that in March he had rebuked Kristi Noem , then Trump’s homeland security secretary, for spending millions in government funds “to bolster her public image” in a $220m series of ads she starred in. She then asked the Louisiana senator to comment on the new ads featuring Trump, which the White House calls “public service announcements”.
“Our viewers are going to see a 30-second commercial on this program,” Brennan said. “It’s on all major networks – it’s on the cable networks as well. It prominently features President Trump, and there’s a voice praising him as ‘the toughest, most resilient person I ever met’. And at the end, it says ‘paid for by the US government’. Is that the best use of taxpayer money?”
Kennedy replied: “Well, first, as to secretary Noem, what she did was masterclass dumb. She spent $220[m] on commercials about her, and I called her out on it.”
“This looks like a commercial about President Trump,” Brennan noted, referring to the first ad in the series , a 30-second highlight reel of Trump’s second presidency, punctuated by on-screen text driving his political agenda and suggesting Democrats are communists.
“I don’t think any public official, including President Trump or Kristi Noem or John Kennedy, should spend public money … on private ads for themselves,” Kennedy replied. “Now, the White House sees it differently. But … I think there ought to be a rule that you can’t – well, there probably is a rule – you can’t spend public money to promote yourself.”
Kennedy, a lawyer with degrees from both the University of Virginia and University of Oxford, appeared to be tacitly acknowledging the argument made by Jamie Raskin, a Democratic congressman and legal scholar, that any government employees who worked on the first pro-Trump ad – “or used government resources to make it” – may have committed a felony violation of the Hatch act , a law that bars government workers from partisan campaign activities.
According to Medium Buying, a company that buys airtime for Republican candidates , the Trump administration used more taxpayer funds to broadcast another partisan ad featuring the president that aired nationwide on Saturday during a college football game between Ohio State and Illinois on Fox. It aired again during Fox News Sunday.
That 30-second spot shows a moody, black-and-white shot of Trump staring into the camera as the soundtrack plays the closing riff of a campaign speech he gave dozens of times in 2023 and 2024.
“This is the final battle,” Trump says in the ad. “With you at my side, we will demolish the deep state; we will expel the warmongers from our government; we will drive out the globalists; we will cast out the communists, Marxists and fascists,” he continues, with cheers from a crowd. Those cheers indicate that the audio was recorded during a campaign rally and at a time before he used his power as president to start a war with Iran that has left some supporters feeling betrayed.
“We will rout the fake news media, and we will liberate our country from these tyrants and villains once and for all,” Trump can be heard promising in language clearly calculated to appeal to Christian supporters by echoing the biblical story of Jesus driving merchants and money changers from the temple in Jerusalem.
The newest ad, with on-screen text reading “Paid for by the US Government”, is even more obviously a partisan product than the first one. In fact, the ad was created for Trump’s 2024 election campaign. And it was posted on his Truth Social account in 2023 and 2024 with a plea for funds from supporters.
after newsletter promotion
The rhetoric was written in to Trump’s standard campaign speech as early as July 2023 , and then repeated by him again and again at dozens of rallies and appeals for donations.
The ad was even played on giant screens during the 2024 Republican national convention before Trump’s speech accepting his party’s nomination. When it was broadcast during the convention by C-SPAN on 18 July 2024, the ad was identified as material “provided by the Republican National Committee”.
At the end of his interview with CBS on Sunday, Kennedy volunteered that he also opposed Trump’s drive to put his own name on public buildings.
“I also think that we ought to have a rule that no politician can have a building named after him while he’s alive,” Kennedy said, before adding that there is such a statute in his home state.
“Well, we’ll watch, Senator, if you introduce that,” Brennan responded.

Aleksandar VuÄiÄ's resignation comes years after more than a year of protests over allegations of government corruption
Serbia's president has resigned after more than a year of student-led protests and growing public discontent over allegations of government corruption.
Aleksandar VuÄiÄ said his administration had preserved peace and stability during his nine-year tenure as he addressed supporters outside the presidential building in the capital, Belgrade.
He had already announced his intention to resign in June and is currently standing to be his party's candidate for prime minister in the upcoming parliamentary elections. VuÄiÄ cannot run for a third presidential term under Serbia's constitution.
The pro-Russian populist's administration has been dogged by anger over alleged corner-cutting.
It was the collapse of the Novi Sad railway station's roof , killing 16 people, that first galvanised anger towards the government in 2024.
Protests involving a wide range of citizens - from students and teachers to workers and farmers - followed.
Demonstrators believed that the disaster reflected more than a decade of governing by the Progressive Party of Vucic, who closely associated himself with the station's renovation, which was supposed to be a symbol of Serbia's progress.
A series of resignations of those under the embattled president failed to placate the protesters, who continued to demonstrate throughout this summer, turning to unrest following accusations of police brutality .
VuÄiÄ's presidency was due to expire next year. Under Serbia's constitution, presidential elections must be held no more than three months after his resignation.
This means Serbians will go to the polls twice before the end of the year.
VuÄiÄ said the presidential election will take place more than a month after the snap parliamentary election in late October, itself called in response to the protests, which had added calls for a vote to their list of demands.
He had earlier announced that he planned to run in that election as Progressive Party's leader, leaving the possibility he could retain a position at the top of Serbian politics.
Parliamentary speaker Ana BrnabiÄ, also a Progressive Party member, will assume the role of interim president until a new one is elected.
VuÄiÄ used his constitutional powers to pardon 49 people, including 23 students and party loyalists suspected of offences related to what he called the "terrible events we have gone through over the past year and a half", according to Serbian public broadcaster RTS.
The upcoming parliamentary elections will pit VuÄiÄ's Progressive Party against a student-led, anti-corruption movement called Students Win and a coalition of pro-Western opposition parties known as European Serbia.
Vucic has been a fixture of Serbian politics for more than a decade , becoming prime minister in 2014, before being elected to his first term as president in 2017.
He has publicly said he wants Serbia to join the EU while courting close ties with Russia and opening Serbia up to Chinese investment.

Coastal communities across the Northeast faced more flooding and power outages on Sunday as a powerful nor’easter continued to lash the region , with forecasters warning that upcoming high tides could further submerge vulnerable shorelines.
The slow-moving storm —which resulted in a fatality on Saturday when a falling tree struck a New York City housing authority worker—was expected to persist through Sunday with heavy rain, high winds, and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.
Positioned south of Long Island and east of northern New Jersey on Sunday morning, the storm was forecast to loop around the region for roughly another 24 hours, said Bob Oravec, a lead forecaster with the National Weather Service in College Park, Maryland.
Meteorologists expected the heaviest remaining rainfall on Sunday to span northern New Jersey through New York City and Long Island into southern New England. While the system was gradually losing strength, Oravec noted that the threat of tidal flooding would persist during morning and evening high-tide cycles.
"The most impactful parts of the storm are likely going to be the high winds and the tidal flooding," Oravec said.
The weather evoked memories of 2012's Superstorm Sandy, which caused over $60 billion in damage across the eastern US. Although the current impact remains far lower, it could mark the first of several East Coast storms this fall influenced by an El Niño climate pattern.
More than 130,000 customers lost electricity across the Northeast and mid-Atlantic by Sunday morning, according to PowerOutage.us.
The most severe outages affected the New Jersey coastline, Long Island, and coastal Connecticut. Fallen trees across Long Island damaged homes and vehicles, blocked roads, and severed power lines.
The Federal Emergency Management Agency stated that regional response centers were operating at an "enhanced posture," with emergency personnel staged in New England in case of widespread blackouts.
On Saturday, flooded streets in New York and New Jersey saw residents kayaking, while others attempted to surf elevated waves at local beaches. Emergency crews in Sea Bright, New Jersey, rescued a woman and her dog trapped in a flooded vehicle, ABC7 reported.
In Surf City, New Jersey, floodwaters entered a marina where staff had relocated equipment, and owner Kenny Formica said clients reported missing boats and Jet Skis blown from lifts. In Norfolk, Virginia, high waters left driving cars pushing wakes through streets.
Travel across the region was also upended. Hundreds of flights were grounded at Boston Logan International Airport, and flooding cut highway access to Hatteras Island, North Carolina, stranding tourists and forcing a couple to relocate their wedding when roughly 45 guests could not reach the island.

The powerful nor’easter lashing Nantucket with wind and rain has uncovered a piece of the island’s maritime history.
A large section of a shipwreck was spotted Saturday along Nantucket’s south shore, near Point of Breakers and the Sewer Beds, where relentless waves have caused significant coastal erosion.
The wooden wreckage is believed to be part of the 19th-century schooner Warren Sawyer, which ran aground near Miacomet Beach on Dec. 22, 1884, the Nantucket Current reported.
The Warren Sawyer wrecked on Nantucket on the night of Dec. 22, 1884, around 11 p.m., loaded with a cargo of cotton and scrap iron.
The section uncovered by the storm sits in the same area where pieces of the Warren Sawyer were exposed in December 2022.
More than a century after the schooner wrecked, the nor’easter’s powerful waves have once again pulled remnants of the vessel from beneath the sand.
The nor’easter hammered the Big Apple over the weekend, bringing coastal flooding, downed trees and power outages across New York City.

A sailboat sits stranded on Wollaston Beach in Quincy, Massachusetts, after breaking loose from its nearby dock during the nor’easter.

Coastal erosion in Stone Harbor, New Jersey.
Stone Harbor isn’t the only stretch of coastline feeling the damaging effects of the relentless nor’easter.
Erosion has worsened along vulnerable shorelines from the Outer Banks to New England as relentless waves from the nor’easter eat away at beaches, dunes and waterfront communities.
Over 40,000 customers across the Northeast were without power as the nor’easter continued to bring strong winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to the region.

Downed trees and power lines have been reported across the Northeast as crews work to restore service while the storm continues to impact the region.
A Massachusetts resident stepped in to help clear a massive downed tree blocking Quaker Highway in Worcester County as the nor’easter continued to batter the region.

“Your help means so much,” officials said, adding that MassDOT likely appreciated the extra assistance as crews worked to keep roads open and safe.
Coastal flooding has inundated dozens of waterfront communities along the East Coast, but the CDC says now is probably not the time to turn your front yard into a swimming hole.
Along the Jersey Shore, one man still took a dip in coastal floodwaters as the nor’easter continued to hammer the East Coast.
The CDC says coastal floodwater can contain human and animal waste, household and industrial chemicals, medical waste, debris, downed power lines and even dangerous wildlife.
Exposure can lead to wound infections, skin rashes, gastrointestinal illness and other diseases.
Coastal flooding can also overwhelm drainage and sewer systems, sending bacteria and pollutants into nearby waterways.

NOAA researchers have found that coastal floodwaters can pick up fecal-indicating bacteria, disease-causing pathogens and chemical contaminants from urban areas.
If you must venture out, trade the swimsuit for a kayak and do your best to stay dry—and out of the floodwater.

articles.content_orig:
Lithuanian Foreign Affairs Minister Kestutis Budrys discusses NATO jets shooting down a drone in Lithuanian airspace as tension rises in the Baltic region. Budrys also calls for continued pressure on Russia.
Finnish and Swedish fighter jets scrambled for the first time on Sept. 24 to intercept supersonic Russian military aircraft flying over the Gulf of Finland, marking a major milestone in Nordic defense cooperation amid heightened tensions with Moscow.
The mission also came one day before Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed European warnings about the threat from Moscow in the region and mocked Estonia's new defense minister over the Baltic state's preparations for a potential Russian attack.
Finnish F/A-18 Hornets and Swedish JAS 39 Gripens were scrambled after Russian aircraft were detected in the international airspace, according to the Swedish Armed Forces .
US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS
Finnish and Swedish fighter jets scrambled for the first time on Sept. 24 to intercept supersonic Russian military aircraft flying over the Gulf of Finland. (AFP PHOTO MICHAL CIZEK (Photo credit should read MICHAL CIZEK/AFP via Getty Images)
The Russian formation included a Tu-134 transport plane, a high-altitude, supersonic MiG-31 interceptors designed to detect and engage long-range threats; and Su-30 multirole fighter jets which are designed for air-to-air and air-to-ground combat.
"This is what close cooperation looks like in practice," Maj. Gen. Jonas Wikman, commander of the Swedish Air Force, said in a statement following the joint operation.
"Built over years on trust and strong personal relationships, we can now operate seamlessly together — as air forces, as nations and as Allies."
Concern over Russian military activity along NATO’s eastern flank has grown following a string of airspace violations.
These include Russian drones entering Polish airspace, a Mi-8 helicopter crossing from Kaliningrad into Poland , drones crashing in Romania and Moldova, and armed Russian jets entering Estonian airspace before being intercepted by NATO aircraft on Sept. 18.
BATTLE-TESTED ZELENSKYY SOUNDS CHILLING ALARM ON WHERE PUTIN’S WAR COULD HEAD NEXT
The Russian formation included Su-30 multirole fighter jets designed for air-to-air and air-to-ground combat. (Sergey Mihailicenko/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images))
In Estonia, Defense Minister Martin Herem warned that Russia could be capable of using military force against Estonia within a year and argued that Tallinn must determine whether its defenses are sufficient for such a scenario.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal stated that the government is ready to shut down border crossing points on short notice if threat assessments change, according to reports .
Speaking at the St. Petersburg International United Cultures Forum on Friday, Putin pushed back against such warnings.
"Many people in Europe say they expect an attack from Russia and therefore claim they must prepare for war with Russia," Putin said.
"I want to emphasize once again: we are not preparing for military action against Europe. We have no such plans, no basis for them, and, most importantly, no real motive to escalate the situation with Europe."
Putin then mocked Herem's warnings: "As we jokingly say in Russia: 'The circus has left, but the clowns remain.' It is political clowning. ... Clearly, these statements are complete nonsense and absurdity," Putin said, according to EurAsia Daily .
FOREIGN LEADER ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP SOUNDS ALARM OVER IRAN FUELING MOSCOW’S WAR MACHINE
Putin spoke at the St. Petersburg International United Cultures Forum and downplayed comments made by Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem, who warned that Russia could be capable of using military force against Estonia. (Alexander KAZAKOV / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
Estonia sits across the Gulf of Finland from Finland, with the three countries forming part of NATO's increasingly integrated northern and eastern defenses amid concerns about Russian military activity.
Finland formally joined NATO as its 31st member in April 2023, roughly doubling the alliance's land border with Russia. Sweden followed as the 32nd member in March 2024. Estonia, which regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, has been a NATO member since 2004.
The Baltic Sea region has also remained on heightened alert following incidents involving gas pipelines, sabotage and hybrid threats since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Reuters has reported.
NATO said in June that it was enhancing protection of its eastern members in the cyber and space domains while helping countries build resilience against what it describes as hostile Russian actions, including cyberattacks, sabotage and airspace violations.
NATO says its military activities along the eastern flank are entirely defensive and that it is "ready, willing and able to defend every Ally."
FINLAND'S STUBB CREDITS TRUMP FOR PUSHING UKRAINE PEACE TALKS WHILE DISMISSING RUSSIAN INVASION FEARS
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte speaks during the launch of the NATO Secretary General's Annual Report for 2025 at NATO headquarters in Brussels, Thursday, March 26, 2026. (Virginia Mayo/AP Photo)
The alliance has said an attack against any member would be met with a "resounding response."
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte recently underscored Washington's role in the alliance during a visit to Iowa, telling The Associated Press that Putin "knows that the United States and Europe are totally intertwined."
"We have to make sure that we are prepared, we are strong, and he knows it," Rutte said.
"And if he does anything silly, he knows our reaction will be tough," he warned.
European intelligence officials said Sept. 24 that Russia could test NATO's defenses.
Denmark's Defense Intelligence Service assessed the risk of a limited Russian military attack against a NATO country in the coming months as "low but growing" and said Moscow is expected to intensify its hybrid campaign against NATO and the West.

The service said in a statement that a full-scale Russian invasion of a NATO member remains highly unlikely but can no longer be ruled out.

PFF's fantasy football recap focuses on player usage and stats, breaking down all the vital information you need to achieve fantasy success in 2026.
Los Angeles uses more of a committee in the backfield: All three of the Chargers' running backs played between 24-42% of snaps.
The Chargers began the season with Omarion Hampton playing a dominant 74.3% of snaps on early downs. Keaton Mitchell saw more time in passing situations, leading Hampton to play 58.2% of snaps in Week 1. In Week 2, Kimani Vidal mixed in a little more in passing situations, and Hampton’s snap rate remained high on early downs.
This week, Vidal worked in even more, leaving Hampton to barely be on the field in passing situations. Mitchell played 38.6% of the early-down snaps, up from 23.7% over the first two weeks. Mitchell was also the more impressive running back in the box score. He totaled nearly as many rushing yards as Hampton despite receiving roughly half the carries, and he caught a touchdown pass.
Over three games, Mitchell has averaged more yards per carry and more yards after contact per carry. While Hampton has the better first-down rate, Mitchell owns the better clip of breaking 5-or-more-yard runs, and Mitchell’s number is more than double Hampton’s on 10- and 15-yard runs. We could see Mitchell’s touches continue to improve, making him a solid waiver option.
Chargers adjust down tight ends: Los Angeles focused its passing game on wide receivers down its top two tight ends.
The Chargers began the season with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar as their two top tight ends, with Njoku playing more on third downs, Kolar on early downs and the two sharing 12 personnel. This left little room for Oronde Gadsden , who was considered a potential fantasy starter at the start of 2026 before Los Angeles made the two free-agent additions. However, Njoku suffered a knee and fibula injury last week, landing him on injured reserve, while Kolar endured a forearm injury, which kept him out of this game and will likely hold him out longer. In response, Los Angeles signed Hayden Rucci , who had experience in Mike McDaniel's offense, and elevated Patrick Herbert , brother of Justin Herbert , off the practice squad.
The rotation was straightforward, with Gadsden taking 25 of 30 snaps out of 11 personnel, while Rucci handled 17 of 24 snaps out of 21 personnel. The two shared the field for all two-tight end sets, with Herbert only seeing one snap on offense out of 13 personnel.
This left Gadsden running a route on a respectable 73.7% of pass plays, but he was only targeted on 7.1% of his routes. He didn’t catch any of his targets. While there is still time to turn things around, Kolar will likely return in the next two or three weeks. This was supposed to be an opportunity for Gadsden to prove he deserves more playing time over the rest of the season, and that didn’t happen in this game.
Ty Johnson makes his 2026 debut: The Bills’ third-down back missed the first two games due to injury.
The Bills spent the first two weeks without their receiving running back. Frank Gore Jr. was a practice squad call-up to take over the third-down and two-minute drill duties. However, Gore didn’t dominate passing-down opportunities in the same way Johnson did, and also didn’t cut into snaps as much on early downs. This led James Cook III to play 85.2% of early-down snaps over the first two weeks, and Ray Davis cut into the passing-down work. Only Jonathan Taylor dominated early snaps more than Cook over the first two weeks of the year.
While Johnson played the clear majority of passing situations and caught four passes, Cook played 81% of snaps on early downs. Part of that was the fact that the Bills were playing from behind for a lot of the game and needed a fourth-quarter comeback. It wouldn’t be surprising if Johnson takes a higher percentage of early-down snaps in games where the Bills have a big lead. Of course, if the Bills hold a major advantage, Cook likely would have played a large role in that, so his fantasy managers shouldn’t worry about his touches even with Johnson back.
Chuba Hubbard dominates touches without Jonathon Brooks : The Panthers' lead running back played 100% of snaps in the first half.
The Panthers have started the season with Hubbard as their clear starter and Brooks as his backup. Third-string running back Trevor Etienne has began the year on injured reserve, with Brooks joining him on Wednesday. Brooks underwent surgery for a core muscle injury, which is expected to keep him out at least six weeks. This left AJ Dillon as the backup running back, while Anthony Tyus III was elevated from the practice squad to be the third back.
Tyus didn’t play at all on offense, and Dillon didn’t see his first offensive snaps until the middle of the third quarter. While it wouldn’t be surprising if Dillon mixes in a little earlier going forward, Hubbard should receive enough volume to make him a must-start every week until Brooks returns, or until the Panthers find an option they are more comfortable with for their RB2.
Monitor Jalen Coker ’s health: Coker left in the third quarter with a quad injury and didn’t return.
Carolina has used Tetairoa McMillan and Coker as its primary wide receivers, with Xavier Legette joining in 11 personnel over the first two weeks. Carolina was already hurting at wide receiver heading into this game, as Legette was inactive with a knee injury and Coker was questionable for the game with an ankle.
In the first half, Brycen Tremayne took over as the third receiver, with John Metchie III also mixing in. Metchie recently took over for Jimmy Horn Jr. as the Panthers' backup slot option. Once Coker left with an injury, Tremayne became the second receiver in 12 personnel, while he and Metchie were more consistently on the field in 11 personnel. David Moore was a practice squad call-up for this game, and he became the fourth receiver.
Despite what happened in this game, if the injury to Coker is serious, then Legette would be the player to pick up off the waiver wire. He was limited in practice on Friday and was questionable going in, making it unlikely Legette’s injury is long-term. He’s been ahead of Tremayne when healthy and would likely take on a full-time role if Coker misses time.
Monitor Mitchell Evans ’ health: The Panthers backup tight end suffered a right arm injury in the fourth quarter and didn’t return.
Carolina has spent the first two weeks with Tommy Tremble and Evans often playing in 12 personnel, Darren Waller as the third-down option and a rotation of the three players in 11 personnel on early downs. That continued in this game, though the Panthers played 11 personnel more often and trusted Waller for a higher percentage of 11 personnel snaps, giving Waller more time and less to Tremble and Evans.
After Evans’ injury, Waller played two snaps in 12 personnel. If Evans injury is serious and he starts to miss time, we could see an uptick in snaps by Waller. Waller’s route participation rate and targets per route have increased each week. While his targets per route is unlikely to augment much more, an uptick in route participation rate would turn Waller into a fantasy starter as long as he stays healthy.

Denzel Boston has been the Browns' X receiver all season, playing over 90% of snaps in 11 and 12 personnel and the majority of 13 personnel snaps, giving him a 91.1% snap rate on the season. articles.title_orig: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive in Atlanta from China - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive in Atlanta from China - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, have arrived in the US state of Georgia on a 10-year loan as a soft-power gesture from China.
A new agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association makes Atlanta one of three zoos in the US to house giant pandas .
The diplomatic gifts departed early on Sunday from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport in southwestern China, according to Chinese state media. They arrived after the high-level three-day Washington summit with China last week, where closed-door talks between United States President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping yielded no major policy breakthroughs on prickly issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran.
Although the pandas’ transfer had been finalised back in April, Xi officially announced the arrival timeline on Thursday at the White House, noting that the black and white mammals could reach Zoo Atlanta from the Chengdu Research Base, China’s premier hub for giant panda conservation, breeding and research, within the next few days. The dispatch of the vulnerable species aimed to signal a renewed bilateral friendship between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies.
Ahead of their arrival, Zoo Atlanta had upgraded its panda habitats and secured a stable, long-term supply of locally grown Atlanta bamboo, which shares a near-identical climate with Chengdu.
The bears completed a 16-hour charter flight across the International Date Line, landing in Atlanta, Georgia, shortly before 7:00am (11:00am GMT).
Midway through its journey through Alaska, the FedEx Boeing 777 had spiked to the top of Flightradar24’s global tracking charts.
Steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots were prepared to keep the pandas nourished during their flight, Chinese state-run media reported. The US also mobilised a specialised care team to accompany the duo on their flight, they said.
A spokesperson for the zoo told Al Jazeera that their team had “done everything possible to accommodate them”, but a definitive timeline for their arrival – much less their public debut – remains “unconfirmed”.
“This is a thrilling day for Zoo Atlanta and a historic moment for the City of Atlanta, the state of Georgia and beyond,” Zoo Atlanta President and CEO Raymond B. King said in a statement. “We are elated to welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and could not be more excited about sharing that joy with our Members, guests, city and community in the coming weeks.”
Zoo visitors will have to wait a while to see Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, officials said. The bears will be quarantined for about a month in a biosecure area of the wildlife park’s new giant panda complex. The zoo last had pandas in 2024.
Ping Ping, a male, and Fu Shuang, a female, were born in 2020.
Globally revered, the iconic furry animals have been sent across the globe for decades, serving as diplomatic emissaries loaned by China under its infamous “panda diplomacy” initiative through soft-power projection. Beijing leverages the animals’ immense public appeal to cultivate international goodwill, seal lucrative trade deals and burnish its geopolitical image abroad. Similarly, when foreign relationships fray or tensions arise, Beijing lets the loan agreements expire.
Xi has said this latest loan programme was an example of “friendship between the Chinese and Americans”.
Last week’s summit was Xi’s first visit to Washington in more than a decade and the second meeting this year with Trump.
Tangible outcomes of the meetings remain modest , restricted to a two-month extension of the trade truce, Beijing’s revival of giant panda loans and Xi’s support for Trump’s rebranding of artificial intelligence as “super intelligence”.

articles.title_zh: Georgia park mass shooting wounds 11 teens at birthday party
articles.content_orig:
Eleven people in their late teens were shot overnight Sunday at a park in Georgia, according to law enforcement.
The Bibb County Sheriff's Office said the shooting occurred around midnight "at a large gathering" in Carolyn Crayton Park in the city of Macon, about 85 miles southeast of Atlanta. The wounded victims were identified as four 18-year-old men, two 18-year-old women and five 17-year-old boys, according to the sheriff's office.
Two of the victims, an 18-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, were in critical condition, authorities said. The others were in stable condition.
The gathering appeared to be a birthday party that was originally supposed to take place at an Airbnb in Jones County, but the host made the group leave the premises, according to Bibb County Sheriff David Davis. The group included several students from nearby Central High School and Northeast High School, Davis said.
After the birthday party attendees gathered at the park, another group arrived and an argument between the two groups escalated into gunfire, Davis told reporters at a news conference.
All the victims were part of the party, Davis added, saying that he "can't remember the last time we've had this many people shot at one time."
No arrests have been made, and an investigation is ongoing.
The FBI is assisting in the investigation due to the number of people involved, but Davis said all the evidence so far indicates the incident is local.

articles.title_orig: Mike Vrabel admits his concern 'is very high' for Patriots after Drake Maye commits 3 turnovers in ugly loss to Jaguars
articles.title_zh: Mike Vrabel admits his concern 'is very high' for Patriots after Drake Maye commits 3 turnovers in ugly loss to Jaguars
articles.content_orig:
A turnover-plagued season for Drake Maye hit a new low on Sunday as he added three more against the Jacksonville Jaguars to take the league lead in giveaways.
The Jags turned those giveaways into 14 points in a 35-6 thrashing .
Maye's first turnover of the day was one for the blooper reel.
The New England Patriots were driving on their second possession in a scoreless game. On first-and-10 from the Jacksonville 35, Maye dropped back for a pass and appeared to be targeting wide receiver Kyle Williams , who had one-on-one coverage on a post route down the right sideline.
But he forgot one thing — to throw the ball. Just before he brought his arm forward to pass, the ball slipped from Maye's hand.
Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton recovered the ball, and a promising Patriots possession was over.
Maye wasn't hit. He wasn't even under pressure. The ball just slipped from his hand. Replay confirmed the call on the field that the ball came loose before his arm moved forward.
Here's another look in slow-motion confirming that the ball was out. Maye said afterward there was blood on the ball, which caused it to slip from his hand.
Making matters worse for the Patriots, the Jaguars converted the turnover into a 10-play, 62-yard touchdown drive for a 7-0 lead.
Unfortunately for Maye and the Patriots, he added to his turnover tally late in the second quarter. With just over a minute remaining in the first half, trailing 14-3, New England had third-and-goal from the Jacksonville 2-yard line. Maye rolled right, looking for Efton Chism III in the back of the end zone but instead found the waiting arms of Travis Hunter. It was the first pick of the second-year, two-way player's career.
Then, in the third quarter, Maye turned the ball over again. This time, cornerback Jarrian Jones jumped a sideline pass targeting Williams and returned it 32 yards to the New England 5-yard line.
Jacksonville scored a touchdown to extend it's lead to 28-3 on the next play as a bad day for Maye and the Patriots continued to get worse.
"I can't get out of my own way, personally," Maye said. "I have to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point.
"We have to realize that what we're doing out there offensively is unacceptable. Starts with myself."
The turnovers were Maye's fifth, sixth and seventh this season and he now has 15 since the start of last season's playoffs in six-plus games. His seven turnovers through three quarters of Sunday's game are the most in the NFL againt just one touchdown.
"My concern level is very high for this football team," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters after the game. "I just wanna coach and improve. I think that's the biggest thing when you come off a game like that. You just wanna get back and work."
By comparison, Maye totaled 11 turnovers in 17 games over the course of the entire 2025 regular season in route to All-Pro honors and a runner-up finish in the MVP race. Until he fixes his turnover issues, the Patriots are going to have a difficult time gaining traction in their quest to repeat as AFC champions.

articles.title_orig: Thinking about buying stocks instead of a home? The S&P 500 has blown away the housing market
articles.title_zh: Thinking about buying stocks instead of a home? The S&P 500 has blown away the housing market
articles.content_orig:
From an investing perspective, U.S. homes have paled in comparison to the stock market in recent years, and the surge in mortgage rates will likely widen that mismatch.
The housing market has been largely frozen since the COVID-era boom ended in 2022, when the Federal Reserve embarked on an aggressive rate-hiking campaign to rein in inflation. The Fed is now tightening policy again, and the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate is back above 7%.
At the same time, the AI boom has supercharged stocks, and the S&P 500 has been on a hot streak of double-digit annual gains not seen since the late 1990s.
That’s not lost on younger Americans, who have been shut out of the housing market. They are choosing to rent and investing in stocks to build wealth rather than saving up for a downpayment on a home they may never be able to afford.
Over the past decade, that has worked out well. From December 2015 through December 2025, the Case-Shiller Index of home prices has increased 87%, while the S&P 500 has soared 235%—and that doesn’t include dividends that boost returns even higher.
For Ray Fisman, an economist at Boston University, and Michael Luca, an economist at Carnegie Mellon University, the split between the housing and stock markets should challenge Americans’ long-held views of homeownership.
“The rent-versus-buy decision involves real trade-offs that too often go unrecognized, especially by those who can comfortably afford to buy,” they wrote in a Wall Street Journal op-ed this past week. “Buying a home also bundles two very important, but very different, decisions: where to live, and how to invest a large chunk of your life savings.”
To be sure, the comparison isn’t totally apples to apples, they acknowledged, pointing out that a home provides a place to live as well as an investment return. The U.S. tax code also has benefits for homeownership.
But even when home prices have seen robust gains, “the returns to buying can be, well, meh,” the economists added.
That’s the case so far in 2026 as well. The latest Case Shiller data shows home prices are up 1.5% nationwide, while the S&P 500 is up 13%, despite the Iran war and fears of an AI bust sending stocks on a wild ride this year.
The ability to borrow may be distorting how homeowners perceive their gains, according to Fisman and Luca. By financing the vast majority of the purchase price while putting only a small portion down in equity, any appreciation magnifies an investment.
For example, a 20% downpayment on a house that goes up by 10% in value translates to a 50% return on their initial equity, they noted.
But a decline in prices similarly has outsized impacts, especially given that a home is a “single, illiquid, undiversified asset.” That’s why financial advisers don’t recommend borrowing hundreds of thousands of dollars to buy a single stock, Fisman and Luca wrote.
They added that they aren’t saying no one should ever buy a home. Ownership has upside, like being able to remodel without a landlord’s permission, while renting has downside, like limited supply and the risk of being forced to move.
“The mistake we see all too often is the tendency to bundle two very different decisions,” Fisman and Luca said. “Where you want to live need not be where you want to invest.”
For those who are thinking more about where to live, however, prospective homeowners currently enjoy a buyer’s market.
Indeed, sellers gave concessions in 44.7% of home sales last month, up 2.1 percentage points from a year ago and the highest share for the month of August since at least 2020, Redfin said in a recent report .
Incentives typically include mortgage rate buy-downs, or sellers agreeing to pay for repairs. To win over increasingly selective buyers, sellers are also offering household appliances, or concessions totaling $10,000 to $20,000.
Some sellers have become so desperate they are also dropping the asking price. One real estate agent in Atlanta even offered their client a free week-long vacation in an Airbnb owned by the home’s seller. Another in Charlotte offered an all-expenses-paid cruise.
“If we were to quantify all these concessions… we would see that home prices are down, and people are getting better deals,” Redfin Chief Economist Daryl Fairweather told Fortune’s Sasha Rogelberg.
Jason Ma is the weekend editor at Fortune , where he covers markets, the economy, finance, and housing.

articles.title_orig: Amodei critics target Trump with hit piece before White House dinner
articles.title_zh: Amodei critics target Trump with hit piece before White House dinner
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei will join President Donald Trump for a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, CNBC confirmed, in what will be the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders.
Amodei was noticeably absent from Trump's glitzy state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, as other tech bigwigs — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg — were photographed rubbing elbows with government officials. Amodei had a scheduling conflict, so Trump invited him to a private dinner, according to a source familiar with the details who was not authorized to speak publicly.
The meeting, first reported by Axios , comes at a high-stakes moment for Anthropic, which is gearing up for what's widely expected to be a blockbuster IPO . The company's precarious relationship with the Trump administration has been under strain for much of the last year, so Amodei's sit-down with the president could serve as a valuable opportunity to ease tensions.
"President Trump has been clear: America will lead the world in Super Intelligence, while protecting American consumers," a White House official said in a statement, in response to CNBC's inquiry about Sunday's dinner. "We will drive innovation, strengthen American competitiveness, and ensure this transformative technology works for the American people."
Amodei drew Trump's ire earlier this month by publicly urging the AI industry to slow down the pace of advanced model development and better address potential risks . He published a three-step proposal and called for additional government oversight, which angered the president even as it gained the support of other industry leaders like Altman and Musk.
"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social . "The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' - and we will continue to do so!"
Amodei was already in a difficult spot with the president, because he supported Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election and was a vocal critic of Trump.
But before Amodei's call for a slowdown rocked the tech sector, Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration appeared to be on the mend.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who temporarily imposed export controls on two of the company's most advanced models in June, told Axios earlier this month that Anthropic is "back on the right side." He also hosted a fireside chat with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina.
Brown, who serves as Anthropic's chief compute officer, has taken on a much more active role in interfacing with the Trump administration in recent months. He reportedly led the company's negotiations with the Commerce Department over its export control directive, replacing Amodei in that role.
"We trust Anthropic," Lutnick said on the sidelines of the event.
That same day, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Director Michael Kratsios told CNBC that the administration was "in a good cadence" with Anthropic. He said the company was "open" and actively sharing models with the government as part of Trump's voluntary AI executive order.
Anthropic has had less success winning over officials at the Department of Defense, however.
Negotiations between the company and the Pentagon spiraled in February after the two sides failed to agree on how the military could use its models. The DOD wanted Anthropic to grant the military unfettered access to its models across all lawful purposes, while Anthropic wanted assurance that its technology would not be used for fully autonomous weapons or domestic mass surveillance.
After talks collapsed, the DOD labeled Anthropic a supply chain risk , an unprecedented move that meant the company purportedly threatened U.S. national security. The designation prevents the U.S. military from using Anthropic's models and blocks defense contractors from using them in their work with the agency.
Anthropic sued the Trump administration in an effort to reverse it's blacklisting, but the company suffered a blow on Friday after a federal appeals court panel in Washington, D.C., upheld the Pentagon's action . The company could still petition for a rehearing, and could also ask the Supreme Court to take the case.
Emil Michael, the DOD's technology chief, celebrated the ruling in a post on X .
"The hammer of justice has smashed @AnthropicAI arguments," Michael wrote on Friday. "They are a Supply Chain Risk to the defense industrial base serving the @DeptofWar. Warfighters will sleep better knowing that no private company will insert their opinions in the chain of command. @SecWar was right!"
Defense Secretary Hegseth accused Anthropic of "duplicity" and argued that the company attempted "to strong-arm the United States military into submission" when negotiations collapsed in February. He reaffirmed that position in a post on X on Friday.
"Confirmed: @AnthropicAI = Supply Chain Risk," Hegseth wrote. The @DeptofWar does what is right for the Country and our Warriors."
